missingPieces: The capstone submission link is a Microsoft OneDrive folder (1drv.ms / onedrive.live.com). It is not machine readable from this environment. WebFetch followed the 1drv.ms redirect to the onedrive.live.com folder view and returned only the 'Microsoft OneDrive' page header with no file listing and no file IDs, because the folder view requires an authenticated browser session to render its contents. None of the four deliverables (D1 findings, D2 exploit chain, D3 report, D4 ethics) could be retrieved or read. There is no Google Drive or Google Docs mirror in the submission to fall back to.
flagReason: Submission hosted on OneDrive, which cannot be read in this environment. All four deliverables are unreadable, so per the read-reliability rule this is cannotAssess, not a low score. A human grader with browser access to the OneDrive folder must open and grade D1-D4 manually.
feedback: I was unable to grade this capstone because the submission is hosted on a Microsoft OneDrive folder (the 1drv.ms link), and OneDrive folder views cannot be read in this grading environment. When I followed the link it redirected to onedrive.live.com and returned only the 'Microsoft OneDrive' page header with no listing of files and no downloadable file identifiers, because that view needs an authenticated browser session to display its contents. As a result I could not open or read any of the four deliverables, the D1 findings table, the D2 exploit chain and CVSS work, the D3 report, or the D4 ethics essay, so I cannot responsibly assign marks to any row. This is recorded as cannot-assess rather than a low score, because a submission I could not read is not the same as weak work, and it would be unfair to penalise content I never saw. To get this graded, please re-host the deliverables somewhere machine readable, ideally a shared Google Drive folder set to 'anyone with the link can view', with each deliverable as its own PDF or Google Doc named clearly D1 Findings, D2 Exploit Chain, D3 Report, and D4 Ethics. If OneDrive must be used, export each file to a direct, publicly viewable download link rather than a folder view. Once the files are readable I or a human grader can score D1 findings out of 30 against the ten-finding key and the hash_equals decoy, D2 exploit chain out of 35 with the capture-line reconciliation and CVSS vectors, D3 report out of 40 with remediation ordered by effort, and D4 ethics out of 15 with the ISC2 canon number and the NDPA 2023 sections 40 and 41. I genuinely could not justify any score here because no deliverable content was accessible, so the single most important next step is to resubmit the four deliverables on a publicly readable link so the work can actually be assessed.
